content: 1. Deutetrabenazine metabolism is influenced by hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors can increase the systemic exposure to its active dihydro-metabolites by approximately threefold. When co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, the dose of deutetrabenazine should not exceed 18 mg per dose and 36 mg per day. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 2. Ritonavir increases dexamethasone levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, dexamethasone decreases ritonavir levels or effects through the same pathway. Ritonavir also increases dexamethasone levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. DHEA (herbal supplement) increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Ritonavir increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Alternatives should be considered if available. 6. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of buccal diazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal diazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 8. Ritonavir enhances the effects of diazoxide through other mechanisms, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Ritonavir and didanosine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Ritonavir decreases didanosine levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Didanosine should be taken one hour before or two hours after lopinavir/ritonavir oral solution administration. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitoring for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache is necessary. 11. Ritonavir increases digoxin levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and reducing renal and hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are required. 12. Diltiazem increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases diltiazem levels or effects through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Ritonavir increases docetaxel levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 14. Ritonavir increases dofetilide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Alternatives should be considered if available. There is an increased risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 15. Ritonavir increases doravirine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Ritonavir increases doxepin levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Ritonavir increases doxorubicin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 18. Ritonavir increases dronabinol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Dronedarone increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Ritonavir increases duloxetine levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Ritonavir increases duvelisib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib AUC, potentially increasing toxicity risk. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 22. Efavirenz decreases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Elagolix increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Elagolix decreases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. CYP3A substrates should be monitored, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 24. Ritonavir increases eletriptan levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Eliglustat increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Therapeutic drug concentrations should be monitored, or the dosage of concomitant drugs should be reduced and titrated to clinical effect. 26. Ritonavir increases eluxadoline levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 27. Ritonavir increases elvitegravir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 28. Ritonavir and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Encorafenib affects ritonavir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage, and MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, raising the risk of enfortumab vedotin toxicities. Close monitoring for signs of toxicity is necessary. 31. Ritonavir and enfuvirtide both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Ritonavir increases erlotinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 33. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Ritonavir increases escitalopram levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. There is a potential for increased toxicity and an elevated risk of serotonin syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 36. Ritonavir increases esomeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 37. Ritonavir increases estradiol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of synthetic conjugated estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 39. Ritonavir increases eszopiclone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. The starting dose of eszopiclone should be reduced to 1 mg/day. 40. Ritonavir increases ethosuximide levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. There is a potential for increased toxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Ritonavir increases etonogestrel levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 42. Ritonavir increases etoposide levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Ritonavir increases etravirine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 44. Ritonavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension through other mechanisms, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Ezogabine and ritonavir may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. The QT interval should be monitored when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Fedratinib increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Dose adjustments of drugs that are CYP2D6 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Ritonavir increases felodipine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Felodipine also increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 48. Ritonavir increases fesoterodine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Fluconazole increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 50. Ritonavir increases fludrocortisone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Fludrocortisone decreases ritonavir levels or effects through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 51. Ritonavir increases flunisolide inhaled levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 52. Ritonavir increases flurazepam levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Alternatives should be considered if available. Lowering the benzodiazepine dose may be necessary. 53. Ritonavir increases fluticasone furoate levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase fluticasone systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Ritonavir increases fluticasone inhaled levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase fluticasone systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 55. Ritonavir increases fluvastatin toxicity through other mechanisms, potentially increasing the risk of myopathy due to OATP1B1 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Fluvoxamine increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 57. Fosamprenavir increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 58. Fosaprepitant increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 59. Fosphenytoin decreases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
